native_metadata.title: A coefficient normalization for positive definite forms
native_metadata.description:
Every positive definite real homogeneous form of positive degree admits an invertible real linear change of variables in which the symmetric ordered coefficients have diagonal entries equal to one and every mixed entry strictly between zero and one. This gives an affirmative answer to Brandes's Problem 11 in the 2019 Oberwolfach report on Analytic Number Theory, including the printed absolute-value inequality.

The three-page proof clusters a basis near a direction minimizing the form on a Euclidean sphere. A polynomial gap has a strictly positive quadratic term for every mixed tuple. The accompanying source package includes an independent proof via positive definite bilinear slices and Cauchy-Schwarz, internal adversarial audits including three fresh preprint-readiness rounds and independently rechecked supplementary controls, a dated priority search, and a standard-library Python verifier with exact rational certificates. The finite checks supplement the analytic proof and are not a formal verification of the universal theorem.

Brandes's 2015 discussion of pseudo-diagonal forms is credited as a direct precursor. A bounded literature audit found no earlier full resolution; first priority is not established. This is an unrefereed preprint developed and checked with generative-AI assistance. Paper and prose: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.

native_metadata.title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
native_metadata.description: For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Their maximal length M(g) is finite and attained, with M(g) ≥ 4g(2g+1). Peripheral factors occur only in the singleton factorization; otherwise all factors are nonseparating. The values M(1) = 12 and M(2) = 40 are credited deductions from prior work with the convention bridge stated. This gives a complete negative answer, under the stated conventions, to the separately printed restricted arbitrary-length clause in the Wajnryb/Farb problem collection. The full original maximum and classification bundle remains partial: exact M(g) for g ≥ 3, explicit upper formulas, an effective exhaustive-enumeration stopping criterion, extremizers, and Hurwitz, positive Artin, T-move and A5/D6 classifications remain unresolved in this work. The note is a credited deduction and exposition. Cossu and Tringali's arXiv:2208.05869v3, Corollary 4.13, supplies the generic finite-alphabet finiteness corollary through a normal reduced cone and nonerasing atomic expansions. The support and ribbon arguments explicitly build on Juvan–Malnič–Mohar, Malestein–Rivin–Theran, and Cahn–Fanoni–Petri. Honda–Kazez–Matić, Smith, the chain relation, and Baykur–Monden–Van Horn-Morris provide credited premises. Exact historical priority of the resulting surface application, novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain UNKNOWN; a bounded literature audit is not an absence proof. Extensive AI tools were used in mathematical and source checking, writing, code, and package preparation. This preprint is unrefereed, has no external human peer review, and is not formally certified. The accompanying verification kit provides written proof and source/custody records plus reproducible finite fault controls; those controls do not replace the universal proof or replay omitted historical inputs.
